title: odis.authz.request.v1
description: Authorization request submitted to the RPV. Mirrors APF §6.2; built by the MCP adapter from a trusted runtime context plus structured tool arguments. Subject fields come from the runtime context, not from caller-supplied tool args. The envelope declares no runtime-risk signal input: ODIS §6.4 types `runtime_risk_signals` as authenticated signal objects the checkpoint MUST validate for issuer trust, integrity, replay resistance, freshness and subject correlation before use, and this harness consumes no such signal.

bundle_id.description: Identifier of the Authority Grant this envelope was produced under. Carried from the loaded grant, not pinned: an envelope must name the grant actually in force.

bundle_version.description: Version of the Authority Grant in force. Carried from the loaded grant, not pinned: an envelope must name the grant actually in force.

trust_root_id.description: Trust anchor the grant's signature chains to. Carried from the loaded grant, not pinned: an envelope must name the grant actually in force.

request_body.description: Structured tool arguments; provider-shaped after MCP adapter normalization.

task_intent.description: Carried verbatim from runtime context; informational, not policy-evaluable. Preserved on authz.request so audit consumers see the agent stated intent at every decision point.

delegation_chain.description: Ordered list of prior delegation hops (ODIS §6.3), empty for a root record. This implementation delegates to no sub-agent — the Router mints one principal-to-agent hop from its identity providers — so the array is constrained empty: `[]` asserts a root record where absence asserts nothing. Hop entries are not modelled, and a claimed hop is refused. §6.3 requires each entry to carry, or integrity-protect a reference to, the identity and authority context needed to verify lineage and attenuation, and its chain validation requires a verifier to digest-match every parent record and check its freshness and revocation state; no revocation channel exists here. `odis.bundle.v1` constrains the same field the same way.

Subject.description: Who the call is on behalf of. `originating_principal` is ODIS §6.3's authenticated initiating principal; `agent` is the acting workload; `delegation_chain` records prior delegation hops and is empty here. All three are required: the Router mints every one of them, so an absent field would mean a Router that failed to state what it knows.
